validation: V4 ZIP hashes/bootstrap/metrics replayed; V3 screening errors recomputed from CSV

figures.title: V3 runtime
figures.explain: The same 10,000 modeled schedules took 672.68 seconds with Radau and 7.93 seconds with my LSTM. Exact Bateman took 0.14 seconds.
figures.caution: These are local CPU measurements of simplified equations. They do not compare supercomputers or full neutron transport. The recorded training-only break-even estimate is about 62,633 predictions versus Radau; it excludes other development costs.

figures.title: V3 matched accuracy
figures.explain: On the specific matched test, my LSTM's reported median was lower than the MLP's. I evaluated four time grids and report the largest grid median.
figures.caution: The result uses a numerical denominator floor and excludes small/zero reference cases. One training seed does not establish a general architectural advantage.

figures.title: V3 screening errors
figures.explain: The median was 3.94%, but the 95th percentile was 183.84%. That means a low typical error did not prevent some very large mistakes.
figures.caution: This is a different task and metric from the matched endpoint test. The productive threshold is 1.8852 Bq. Excluded near-zero cases have separate diagnostics in the frozen JSON.

figures.title: V4 rate errors
figures.explain: LSTM has a slightly lower median; GP has a slightly lower 95th percentile. The paired uncertainty analysis cannot reliably separate their p95 performance.
figures.caution: These are two reaction-rate errors per family, pooled across 48 families. They are not 96 independent experiments or a measurement of real Ac-225 production accuracy.

figures.title: V4 uncertainty coverage
figures.explain: The GP's original bands covered both reference rates in just one of 48 cases. After calibration, both methods covered both rates in 46 of 48 cases.
figures.caution: Raw LSTM uncertainty combines ensemble variation and an error floor. Neither the raw bands nor calibrated intervals include every experimental or nuclear-data uncertainty.

figures.title: V4 domain checks
figures.explain: A separate input checker stopped all 184 deliberately outside-range cases. That is why neither model should be trusted just because it returns a number.
figures.caution: Bounds and training-distance checks cannot detect every kind of distribution change. These results do not establish accurate extrapolation or a universal safety guarantee.

figures.title: V4 Ac-225 propagation
figures.explain: I passed each model's reaction rates into the exact decay equations. This shows how errors in those rates affect the resulting amount of Ac-225.
figures.caution: Three schedules of the same proxy families do not establish real production accuracy. This test is separate from the V3 trajectory and runtime experiments.
